area: permissions, permission modes, auto mode classifier, sandbox, server-managed/managed settings (as of 2026-11-03)

facts.behavior: Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match determines the outcome and specificity does not change the order. A broad deny like Bash(aws *) blocks calls that also match a narrower allow. A matching ask rule prompts even when a more specific allow matches.
facts.limits: An allow rule cannot carve an exception out of a deny. Deny at any scope beats allow at any other scope, and a managed deny cannot be overridden by --allowedTools; --disallowedTools can add restrictions.

facts.feature: Rules are enforced by Claude Code, not the model
facts.behavior: "Instructions in your prompt or CLAUDE.md shape what Claude tries to do, but they don't change what Claude Code allows."
facts.limits: CLAUDE.md guidance is advisory and does not enforce a boundary. A conversational boundary (e.g. 'don't push') in auto mode is not stored as a rule and context compaction can drop it; use a deny rule for a hard guarantee.

facts.feature: Bare tool-name deny removes the tool
facts.behavior: A bare tool name (Bash, Bash(*), or a glob like mcp__*) in deny removes the tool from Claude's context entirely. A scoped deny like Bash(rm *) leaves the tool and blocks matching calls. Tool-name globs work in deny/ask rules; allow globs only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix.
facts.limits: EndConversation cannot be removed or prompted while any other tool remains. Unanchored allow globs ('*', 'B*', 'mcp__*') are skipped and approve nothing. Deny/ask rules naming no known tool give a startup warning.

facts.behavior: Format is Tool or Tool(specifier); parentheses inside the specifier are literal. Canonical tool names are required; labels shown in the transcript (e.g. 'Stop Task' vs TaskStop) do not match.
facts.limits: Write(path), NotebookEdit(path), Glob(path), MultiEdit(path) rules are accepted but never match; use Edit(path) and Read(path).

facts.behavior: Deny and ask rules can match a top-level scalar input parameter on any built-in tool, e.g. Agent(model:opus), Agent(isolation:worktree), Bash(run_in_background:true). * wildcard supported; exact literal match before normalization; omitted params never match.
facts.limits: Cannot match primary content fields (command, file_path, path, notebook_path, url); Bash(command:rm *) is ignored with startup warning. Not usable in allow rules. Nested fields not matchable. For MCP tools, settings-file rules with parentheses (mcp__...(...)) are skipped; use --disallowedTools for parameter rules on MCP tools.

facts.behavior: mcp__<server> or mcp__<server>__* matches all tools of a server; mcp__<server>__<tool> matches one tool. Special characters in server names become _. Plugin servers use mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__*. Deny mcp__* denies every MCP tool.
facts.limits: Rules match tool names only; a settings-file MCP rule with parentheses (argument/parameter constraint) is skipped, so permission rules cannot see inside MCP tool arguments from settings files (only --disallowedTools param rules). Org 'ask' connector tools prompt on every call even in auto and bypassPermissions, and are denied in dontAsk; allow rules don't take effect for them. MCP tools marked requiresUserInteraction still prompt even if a hook returns allow. In Cowork, Bash/WebFetch deny rules also apply to mcp__workspace__bash/web_fetch but Bash allow rules never carry over.

facts.behavior: * in a Bash rule matches any text including spaces. Rule with no * is an exact command. Trailing ' *' also matches the bare command (Bash(ls *) matches ls but not lsof; Bash(ls*) matches lsof). :* suffix is equivalent to trailing ' *' and only recognized at pattern end.
facts.limits: Put * after the subcommand; Bash(git * main) matches any git subcommand incl. -c. Startup warning for allow rule with * before subcommand.

facts.behavior: Recognized separators: &&, ||, ;, |, |&, &, newlines. Every subcommand must be allowed for a compound command to run without prompt. Deny and ask rules apply if any subcommand matches, including inside subshells, command substitution, and control-flow bodies (e.g. ask Bash(git clean *) prompts for echo "$(git clean -f)" even in auto mode). 'Yes, don't ask again' saves a rule per subcommand, up to 5.
facts.limits: A trailing && or || makes the command unparseable and allow rules don't approve it.

facts.feature: Wrapper stripping before Bash rule match
facts.behavior: Fixed set stripped: timeout, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, noglob, flagless xargs, and leading known-safe env var assignments. A deny/ask rule matches past any leading env assignment; an allow rule only past known-safe ones.
facts.limits: List not configurable. direnv exec, devbox run, mise exec, npx, docker exec are NOT stripped, so Bash(devbox run *) matches any inner command. xargs with flags is matched as xargs. Exec wrappers (watch, setsid, ionice, flock) and find with -exec/-delete/-rm/-fprint/-files0-from cannot be auto-approved by a prefix rule.

facts.feature: What a Bash deny/ask rule does not match
facts.behavior: Rules match the command text as Claude writes it. Bash(curl *) stops 'curl ...' but not /usr/bin/curl or sh -c 'curl ...'; Bash(rm *) not /bin/rm or bash -c; Bash(git push *) not git -C . push, git -c ... push, git 'push'.
facts.limits: "a deny or ask rule covers the invocation Claude usually produces and isn't a security boundary around the program." Argument-constraining patterns (e.g. curl URL) are fragile (options, redirects, variables). Use sandbox for enforcement independent of command text, or a PreToolUse hook.

facts.behavior: Built-in set (ls, cat, echo, pwd, head, tail, grep, find, wc, which, diff, stat, du, cd, read-only git forms, etc.) runs without prompt in every mode. Unquoted globs permitted when every flag is read-only.
facts.limits: Not configurable; add ask/deny to require prompt. Still prompts for: unquoted globs with write-capable flags, docker pointed at another daemon, file -m/-f, ps with e option, UNC paths on Windows, writes to PATH/IFS, unparseable commands, commands over 10,000 chars, cd+git into different directory, cd+redirect.

facts.behavior: Output redirect targets (>, >>, 2>) are checked against Edit allow/deny rules, protected paths and working directories; input redirects (<) against Read rules (v2.1.257+); tee targets checked (v2.1.269+). Targets starting with ~ or containing glob need approval.
facts.limits: /dev/null, fd forms (2>&1), here-docs/strings not checked. Bash(git commit *) allows the command, not the redirect target.

facts.behavior: Edit rules apply to all built-in tools that edit files. Read rules are applied on a 'best-effort' basis to Grep, Glob, @file mentions, IDE selection/open-file context, pasted image paths, directory listings. Read/Edit deny also applies to recognized Bash file commands (cat, head, tail, sed, tee) and redirect targets. A Read deny also blocks Edit/Write on the same path (Write check v2.1.228+).
facts.limits: Do not apply to commands that read without naming files (grep -r pattern .) or arbitrary subprocesses (a Python/Node script opening files). NotebookEdit not covered by Read deny; add Edit deny. .claudeignore has no effect. For OS-level enforcement use the sandbox.

facts.behavior: gitignore syntax. //path = absolute; ~/path = home; /path = relative to settings source (project/local: primary working dir; user: ~/.claude; --settings file: file's dir; CLI: primary working dir); path or ./path = cwd. Allow Edit(src/**) matches only <cwd>/src; deny/ask Read(secrets/**) matches a secrets dir at any depth. Bare filenames match at any depth. ! negation carves out earlier rules from the same source.
facts.limits: /Users/alice/file is NOT absolute (use //). A user-settings Read(/secrets/**) blocks ~/.claude/secrets, not project secrets. ! carve-outs only reach same-source rules, cannot reach //,~/,/ anchored rules, and cannot reopen a file inside a wholly blocked directory. Windows paths normalized to POSIX form.

facts.behavior: Permission check covers both the requested path and the resolved target. Allow rules need both to match; deny rules apply if either matches. On macOS/Linux a deny/ask rule via a symlinked dir also applies at the real location (v2.1.268+). Edit/Write refuse writes where the path itself is a symlink and direct Claude to the target; unresolvable/looping paths are refused; tools re-confirm path before opening.
facts.limits: Writes can still pass through a symlinked intermediate directory or a Bash/PowerShell command; those resolving outside working dirs aren't auto-approved in acceptEdits, and in auto mode prompt the user unless an allow rule approves; those resolving to a protected path prompt.

facts.behavior: Reads via Read/Grep/Glob of UNC paths (Windows) or /net automount paths get their own prompt. From v2.1.292 allow rules (even bare Read), PreToolUse allow hooks, and the auto-mode classifier do not skip the prompt.
facts.limits: dontAsk denies; bypassPermissions (and interactive plan with bypass available) runs without the prompt. Network paths cannot be added as working dirs.

facts.behavior: WebFetch(domain:example.com) matches hostname, case-insensitive; *.example.com matches subdomains at any depth but not apex; domain:* matches every domain. Mid-pattern wildcards match only text between dots (needs v2.1.172+). Bare WebFetch allow = fetch without prompt; bare WebFetch deny removes the tool. WebFetch(domain:*) in allow/deny also adds/denies the domain for sandboxed commands.
facts.limits: Bare WebFetch does not change sandbox allowed hosts. Bare WebFetch deny/ask does not apply to artifact reads; a domain: rule covering claude.ai or *.claudeusercontent.com does. "using WebFetch alone doesn't prevent network access" if Bash is allowed.

facts.behavior: Agent(Explore)/Agent(Plan)/Agent(custom) in deny disables specific subagents. Cd(path) rules control only the user-typed /cd command: bare Cd deny disables /cd; any Cd allow switches to allowlist mode.
facts.limits: Cd is not model-invocable; rules apply only when the user runs /cd.

facts.behavior: PreToolUse hooks run before the permission prompt for every tool except EndConversation. A hook returning allow does NOT bypass deny or ask rules (deny still blocks, ask still prompts). A hook exiting with code 2 blocks the call before permission rules are evaluated, even if an allow rule matches.
facts.limits: In plan mode a hook allow has no effect on non-read-only calls (except ExitPlanMode). Hook allow does not skip prompts for requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, network-path reads, org-ask connector tools, or critical-path rm. Hooks run commands outside the sandbox. Installed mods' tool.check can approve calls a deny rule refused unless managed settings or a Team/Enterprise /login are present.

facts.behavior: Default access is the launch directory; extend with --add-dir, /add-dir, or permissions.additionalDirectories. Files there follow the same rules as the original working directory; reads need no prompt there.
facts.limits: Project-settings allow rules and additionalDirectories apply only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted (deny/ask are not gated). Trust dialog is interactive only; claude -p / SDK skip project allow rules with a stderr warning. Hooks, env, apiKeyHelper and .mcp.json in the repo are used in -p/SDK without trust.

facts.behavior: When true, file tools refuse reads (or Write/Edit/NotebookEdit writes, v2.1.314+) outside working directories in every permission mode, including bypassPermissions.
facts.limits: Writes key covers only Write, Edit, NotebookEdit; it does not limit shell commands, MCP tools, or hook programs (use sandboxing). Exempts files Claude Code itself needs (e.g. plan files). Reads key also makes sandboxed commands denied read access to home and mounted volumes.

facts.behavior: default (Manual; reads only), acceptEdits (edits + mkdir/touch/rm/rmdir/mv/cp/sed in working dirs and additionalDirectories), plan (read/explore; edits blocked until plan approved), auto (classifier reviews actions), dontAsk (auto-denies anything that would prompt; allow rules and PreToolUse approvals still run), bypassPermissions (skips prompts and safety checks).
facts.limits: Deny rules block in every mode including bypassPermissions; allow rules have no effect in bypassPermissions. dontAsk is not in Shift+Tab cycle and cloud sessions ignore defaultMode dontAsk from settings. dontAsk still denies AskUserQuestion, explicit ask-rule matches, org-ask connector tools, requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, network-path reads, critical-path rm even if allowed.

facts.behavior: "Disables prompts and safety checks, including writes to protected paths." Enter via --permission-mode bypassPermissions, --dangerously-skip-permissions, or permissions.defaultMode in user/--settings/managed settings. First launch shows a warning dialog.
facts.limits: Still prompts/denies: explicit ask rules, org-ask connector tools, AskUserQuestion/requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, critical-path rm/rmdir, 'Dangerous rm operation not ruled out' commands, cross-session messaging safeguards, and outside-working-dir reads/writes when the block settings are on. Refused as root/sudo on Linux/macOS unless in a sandbox, and with --restricted. 'bypassPermissions' in project or local settings is ignored. No protection against prompt injection. Admins block with permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable" (works from any scope).

facts.behavior: Writes to protected directories (.git, .config/git, .vscode, .idea, .husky, .cargo, .devcontainer, .yarn, .mvn, .claude with exceptions, --plugin-dir dirs, ~/.claude/dev-mods/) and files (.gitconfig, .gitmodules, shell rc files, .npmrc/.yarnrc.yml etc., .bazelrc, .pre-commit-config.yaml, lefthook.yml, .devcontainer.json, .ripgreprc, pyrightconfig.json, .mcp.json, .claude.json, managed settings files, files passed via --settings/--mcp-config/--agents) are never auto-approved. default/acceptEdits prompt; plan allowed only in interactive plan with bypass available else classifier/prompt; auto routes to classifier; dontAsk denies; bypassPermissions allows.
facts.limits: permissions.allow rules do not pre-approve protected-path writes. In --restricted sessions the classifier cannot approve them. Not an OS control (sandbox separately denies writes to many of these).

facts.behavior: rm/rmdir on filesystem root, top-level dirs, home, working directory and parents, Windows drive roots, variable-derived targets ("$VAR"/*), command-substitution forms, nested sh -c, etc. prompt or are denied per mode: default/acceptEdits/plan ask; auto asks in terminal with a two-minute countdown (denies elsewhere); dontAsk denies; bypassPermissions asks in terminal. Mounted-drive paths (/Volumes, /mnt, /media) have a separate prompt.
facts.limits: No allow rule, sandbox auto-allow, or PreToolUse allow approves it. "the check can miss commands, so it isn't an OS control"; sandbox limits writes but doesn't stop deleting the working directory. Disable only via launch-environment env vars (not settings env): CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_SUBSTITUTION_RM_PROMPT, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_INLINE_SHELL_RM_PROMPT, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUNTED_DRIVE_RM_PROMPT, CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1 (v2.1.311+, bypass only). Headless -p/SDK auto mode denies; bypass defers to --permission-prompt-tool/canUseTool. PowerShell Remove-Item on system paths/wildcards is denied in every mode.

facts.behavior: Auto-approves file edits and mkdir, touch, rm, rmdir, mv, cp, sed (with safe env prefixes/wrappers) in working directory and additionalDirectories only.
facts.limits: Still prompts for out-of-scope paths, symlinks resolving outside scope, protected paths, critical-path removals, touch with options/globs, and other Bash commands beyond read-only set.

facts.behavior: Claude researches and proposes; edits blocked until plan approved. Shell commands: in interactive terminal with bypass available no prompt; with auto available and useAutoModeDuringPlan (default on) the classifier reviews; otherwise commands outside read-only set prompt even with sandbox auto-allow.
facts.limits: PreToolUse hook allow and mod approvals cannot approve non-read-only calls in plan mode (except ExitPlanMode); sandbox auto-allow substitution for a bare Bash ask rule is skipped.

facts.feature: Auto mode availability and starting mode
facts.behavior: Available on all plans; on Team/Enterprise on by default; admins disable with permissions.disableAutoMode: "disable" (any settings file). Requires supported model (Anthropic API: Opus 4.6+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5 or Fable; Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry: Sonnet 5+, Opus 4.7+, Haiku 5.5 or Fable). Built-in default is auto for interactive terminal and VS Code on v2.1.283+, but Manual for claude -p / Agent SDK (v2.1.302+) and HIPAA configurations. Precedence: --permission-mode flag, then permissions.defaultMode, then built-in default.
facts.limits: "auto" in .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json is ignored (put in ~/.claude/settings.json). If selected but unavailable the session starts in Manual. Anthropic may disable it server-side for the session.

facts.behavior: First match wins: (1) allow/ask/deny rules resolve immediately (exceptions: protected-path writes still go to classifier; critical-path rm ignores allow; requiresUserInteraction MCP and org-ask tools prompt; ask rules matching command content prompt; network-path reads prompt); (2) read-only actions and in-working-dir edits auto-approved; (3) everything else goes to the classifier. On block Claude receives the reason (often naming a rule like [Data Exfiltration]).
facts.limits: Classifier inputs are user messages, non-read-only tool calls, and CLAUDE.md; tool results are stripped. A PostToolUse hook's classifierContext can annotate results (v2.1.236+). Classifier failure (refusal/unparseable) = blocked without notification. Reduces prompts but 'doesn't guarantee safety'.

facts.feature: Broad allow rules dropped in auto mode
facts.behavior: On entering auto mode, Bash(*), PowerShell(*), wildcarded interpreters (Bash(python*)), package-manager run commands, Agent allow rules and Monitor allow rules are dropped; narrow rules like Bash(npm test) stay. Restored on leaving auto.
facts.limits: Deny and ask rules are unaffected; autoMode.classifyAllShell (user or managed) sends every shell command through the classifier even if a narrow allow matches.

facts.feature: Auto mode default block/allow lists and customization
facts.behavior: Blocks by default: curl|bash, sending sensitive data externally, production deploys, IAM grants, force push, git reset --hard/clean -fd/stash drop, amend of pushed commits, terraform destroy, DNS/TLS changes, merging unapproved PRs, disabling CI, credential printing, --dangerously-skip-permissions loops, etc. Allows by default: local working-dir file ops, installing declared deps, reading .env and sending creds to matching API, read-only HTTP, pushing to current repo branches (except deploy-like names). `claude auto-mode defaults` prints the lists. autoMode.environment extends trusted infra, autoMode.allow overrides blocks (user or managed scope).
facts.limits: Project settings cannot set autoMode (User or managed only). Classifier can produce false positives (/feedback). For a human checkpoint add permissions.ask rules. Approvals must name the specific action and dangerous detail; they cover that action only. Full autoMode field semantics (environment/allow/soft_deny/hard_deny) are on auto-mode-config.md, not read.

facts.feature: Auto mode fallback and headless behavior
facts.behavior: Blocked action gives notification and /permissions > Recently blocked entry. 3 consecutive or 20 total blocks pauses auto mode and resumes prompting (fixed thresholds). Headless -p without --permission-prompt-tool: blocked action doesn't run and the run continues. Server-side review may replace classifier calls; no verdict = denied; ten consecutive no-verdict responses stop the turn. Subagents are checked at spawn, per action (subagent permissionMode frontmatter ignored), and on return report.
facts.limits: Classifier model default Sonnet 5; override via CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL (v2.1.302+); unsupported override fails checks and denies. Classifier calls count toward tokens on Enterprise/API/cloud providers and add latency. Reading outside working dirs: first read prompts when blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories off; no prompt in -p/background.

facts.behavior: permissions.allow/ask/deny/additionalDirectories/defaultMode/disableBypassPermissionsMode/disableAutoMode/blockReads...OutsideWorkingDirectories/blockWrites... are 'Any file' scope. autoMode, skipAutoPermissionPrompt are user or managed; skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt user/local/managed; useAutoModeDuringPlan user/local/managed; allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly managed only.
facts.limits: Only the index table of settings-reference was readable; per-key full entries beyond allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly were not visible.

facts.behavior: "Make managed settings the only settings source of permission rules. Claude Code then ignores allow, ask, and deny rules in user, project, local, and --settings files, ignores --allowedTools, hides the always-allow choices in permission prompts, and stops saving new rules." Also ignores allowed-tools frontmatter in skills/commands from repo, ~/.claude, --add-dir and inline plugins (v2.1.282+).
facts.limits: --disallowedTools and the current session's deny/ask rules still apply (only restrict). Embedding-host parent settings: allow rules and additionalDirectories dropped, deny/ask kept. Managed scope only.

facts.behavior: Managed settings are highest; "no other level, including command line arguments, can override a managed permission rule." Deny at any level cannot be allowed by another. Managed-only keys (e.g. allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, managedSourcesBehavior, policyHelper, strictPluginOnlyCustomization, requiredMinimumVersion) are read only from managed settings.
facts.limits: A few security-sensitive keys are exceptions to managed precedence (see settings.md#exceptions-to-managed-settings-precedence, not fetched). Embedding hosts may supply extra managed policy via SDK managedSettings unless allowManaged*Only locks are set.

facts.behavior: "A boundary that the operating system enforces around the shell commands Claude runs": Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands and the processes they start (subagent Bash is sandboxed with the parent's config; background sessions if their settings enable it). Built on @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime. Off by default; enable with /sandbox or sandbox.enabled: true.
facts.limits: "Claude's file tools, MCP servers, and hooks run outside it." Read/Edit/Write/WebFetch/WebSearch follow permission rules instead. Command hooks, local MCP servers, plugin monitors, LSP servers, status line command, apiKeyHelper, mod-started processes run with full access. The ! shell-mode prompt, excludedCommands and unsandboxed retries are unsandboxed. Computer use runs on the real desktop. Not a complete isolation boundary.

facts.behavior: macOS (Seatbelt), Linux and WSL2 (bubblewrap; needs bubblewrap and socat).
facts.limits: "On native Windows, Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed." WSL1 unsupported.

facts.feature: Sandbox failure behavior when it cannot start
facts.behavior: Default: if the sandbox can't start (missing dependency, unsupported platform) Claude Code runs commands without sandboxing. sandbox.failIfUnavailable: true makes Claude Code exit at startup; mid-session failures refuse commands ('Sandbox is required...') and the refused command does not run unsandboxed.
facts.limits: Default is fail-open. On native Windows failIfUnavailable makes Claude Code exit.

facts.behavior: Writes default to working directory, per-user temp dir and added dirs; protected paths (.claude settings, .mcp.json, shell rc, .gitconfig, .vscode/.idea, .git/hooks, .git/config, ~/.claude) stay write-denied. Reads default to "most of the machine, including credential files such as ~/.ssh and ~/.aws/credentials". Keys: filesystem.allowWrite/denyWrite/denyRead/allowRead; sandbox paths use /abs and ~/ (not // as in permission rules). permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories denies reads of home and mounted volumes. credentials.files/envVars with mode deny or mask.
facts.limits: Reads are broad by default unless denyRead is configured. filesystem.disabled turns off filesystem isolation (user/managed/--settings only). Protected-path protection is lost if allowNestedUserNamespaces is enabled.

facts.behavior: No direct route out: Linux uses a separate network namespace, macOS Seatbelt blocks all but a local proxy. Proxy checks hostname against network.allowedDomains (start empty) and deniedDomains; unlisted hosts prompt unless network.strictAllowlist (v2.1.219+). WebFetch(domain:*) rules merge into the sandbox allowlist. Loopback/link-local-only hostnames (169.254.169.254) refused; localhost allowed. Per-command allowed domains in auto mode (v2.1.271+) go to the classifier.
facts.limits: Proxy "does not terminate or inspect TLS"; hostname-based, so domain fronting is possible and broad domains like github.com allow exfiltration paths. Tools ignoring proxy vars (plain ssh, DB drivers) can't connect; UDP/QUIC/ICMP blocked. Custom httpProxyPort/socksProxyPort bypasses Claude Code's domain controls. allowUnixSockets (e.g. docker.sock) can enable bypass.

facts.behavior: When a command fails in the sandbox Claude may retry with dangerouslyDisableSandbox. Approval: bypassPermissions none; Manual/acceptEdits prompt 'Bash command (unsandboxed)'; auto classifier; dontAsk denied. A matching allow rule (e.g. Bash(curl *)) approves with no prompt; an ask rule on Bash(dangerouslyDisableSandbox:true) forces a prompt. sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands: false = strict mode, retry ignored.
facts.limits: Default allows the retry. Strict mode must be set to be effective; managed allowUnsandboxedCommands: false makes sandbox admin-required so repo settings cannot loosen it.

facts.behavior: Defaults true: sandboxed Bash commands run without prompting, independent of permission mode, even with a bare Bash ask rule (sandbox boundary substitutes). false = regular permissions mode with prompts.
facts.limits: Still applies: Bash deny rules, content-scoped ask rules (Bash(git push *)), critical-path rm prompts; skipped in plan mode; Monitor not auto-approved; forms like FOO=bar npm test and eval go through normal flow. Excluded commands respect the bare Bash ask rule.

facts.behavior: Matching commands (Bash rule syntax, e.g. 'docker compose *') run with "no filesystem restrictions and no network proxy" and go through the regular permission flow.
facts.limits: Every command in a chain must match; textual match (a script/make target calling docker internally doesn't match); "An excluded command runs with your full access." Broad patterns on interpreters let Claude write a file then run it unsandboxed. Repo settings cannot add excludedCommands in admin-required sandbox.

facts.behavior: Managed sandbox block can set enabled, failIfUnavailable, allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, allowManagedDomainsOnly, allowManagedReadPathsOnly, and false for weakening keys (enableWeakerNestedSandbox, enableWeakerNetworkIsolation, allowLocalBinding, allowAllUnixSockets, allowAppleEvents, allowNestedUserNamespaces). Admin-required sandbox is triggered by allowUnsandboxedCommands:false or allowManagedDomainsOnly:true; repo .claude/settings*.json then can't loosen it. Server-managed delivery of sandbox.bwrapPath/socatPath/ripgrep, tlsTerminate, proxy ports, credentials, allowApple Events etc. requires user approval dialog.
facts.limits: Managed settings can't stop a developer typing commands at the ! prompt (unsandboxed in most sessions). Sandbox doesn't run on native Windows, so failIfUnavailable exits there.

facts.behavior: Org Owners/Primary Owners configure JSON in claude.ai Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings (Teams/Enterprise). Clients fetch at startup and poll hourly; all settings.json keys supported (hooks, env, managed-only keys like allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly) except OS-policy-only keys (policyHelper, wslInheritsWindowsSettings). Highest settings tier; first source delivering a policy key wins within managed tier (server first, then endpoint), with per-key exceptions (cross-source lock keys, env merging, allowedProviders, login keys).
facts.limits: Applies uniformly to all users (no per-group). No managed-mcp.json via server (use allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers/managedMcpServers v2.1.259+). Needs direct api.anthropic.com and a Team/Enterprise OAuth login, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, or direct API key; Console API keys belong to a different org so don't receive it; skipped when CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* provider vars or non-default ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL are set; not fetched in Cowork. apiKeyHelper/WIF credentials don't trigger fetch.

facts.feature: Server-managed settings fail-open default and forceRemoteSettingsRefresh
facts.behavior: If the startup fetch fails Claude Code continues with cached settings, or without server-managed settings if none cached (warns interactively); endpoint-managed settings still apply. First launch waits up to 5 s for the fetch when signing in. forceRemoteSettingsRefresh: true makes the CLI block at startup until a fresh fetch and exit if it fails (claude auth subcommands exempt); self-perpetuating via cache.
facts.limits: Without it there is a window at startup with no restrictions; hourly background refresh is fail-open. Honored from any admin-controlled managed source (MDM/file) too, which covers first launch. Gateway-signed-in clients exit on failed fetch regardless.

facts.behavior: Settings that execute commands or weaken isolation (apiKeyHelper, statusLine, otelHeadersHelper, sandbox binary/network/isolation settings, risky env vars like proxy/base-URL, any hook definition) require explicit user approval in interactive sessions; rejection makes Claude Code exit. claudeMd delivery needs no approval (v2.1.260+).
facts.limits: Non-interactive runs (claude -p, SDK, VS Code chat panel, desktop Code tab) cannot show the dialog: delivered settings apply for that run only and are not recorded or cached. An interactive session that can't show the dialog keeps last-approved settings.

facts.feature: Server-managed settings are not a security boundary
facts.behavior: "Server-managed settings provide centralized policy enforcement, but they operate as a client-side control, not a security boundary." Cached file at ~/.claude/remote-settings.json can be edited (tampered file applies until next fetch, except withheld env categories); older versions or modified binaries bypass; third-party provider config bypasses; deleting the cache returns to first-launch behavior.
facts.limits: Endpoint-managed (MDM/managed-settings.json) gives stronger guarantees because the file can be OS-protected, but doesn't reach cloud sessions. ConfigChange hooks do not fire when server-managed settings arrive/refresh or MDM changes, and a hook can't block a policy_settings change. Bash(curl *) deny in managed settings matches only 'curl' as written; pair with sandbox allowManagedDomainsOnly.

facts.behavior: On partial schema failure Claude Code surfaces an error and applies remaining valid settings (v2.1.169+); fail-closed keys keep stricter values; cache keeps dropped entries dropped. If every setting fails and none falls back stricter, nothing is applied and cache unchanged (reported by claude doctor, /status).
facts.limits: Admin console schema can lag releases and 'Update with errors' still saves. Verify with claude doctor 'Managed settings (remote)' line (v2.1.248+) and /permissions.

facts.feature: Nested-output and subagent/session interactions with modes

facts.behavior: default (clears override, not itself an alias), best (what fable resolves to where available, else opus), fable, sonnet, opus, haiku, sonnet[1m]/opus[1m]. facts.behavior: Levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max. facts.feature: Output style: what it is and how it applies to the system prompt
facts.behavior: 'An output style is a set of instructions that sets Claude's role, tone, and response format for every response in a session.' Default = no style instructions. Each non-default built-in keeps Claude Code's software-engineering instructions and adds its own. Claude Code 'sends the active style's instructions with every request'. Custom styles on the full system prompt omit Claude Code's built-in software engineering section unless keep-coding-instructions: true. So a custom style replaces part of the system prompt; built-ins add to it.
facts.limits: 'It doesn't guarantee that something always happens or never happens.' / 'it's an instruction Claude follows, so nothing enforces it.' Docs point to CLAUDE.md for project knowledge and hooks for guaranteed behavior. keep-coding-instructions has no effect on the shorter system prompt; set CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT=0 to get the full prompt. Style instructions add input tokens (cache-reduced).

facts.behavior: Four besides Default: Proactive (starts work, assumes on routine decisions, no plan mode unless asked, asks in conversation before destructive/shared/prod actions), Concise (v2.1.237+; leads with result, no preamble/recap, 1-3 sentences for simple questions), Explanatory (Insight blocks in conversation, not in files), Learning (Insight blocks plus TODO(human) code for the user to write).
facts.limits: Proactive does not change permission mode; its check-before-destructive step is an instruction, separate from permission prompts. Concise still gives full detail on request and for safety-relevant output.

area: memory, slash commands, .claude directory, context window (Claude Code docs as of 2026-11-03)

facts.behavior: "Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead." CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt; "there's no guarantee of strict compliance, especially for vague or conflicting instructions." Hooks "execute as shell commands at fixed lifecycle events and apply regardless of what Claude decides to do." Settings rules are "enforced by the client regardless of what Claude decides"; CLAUDE.md is "not a hard enforcement layer."
facts.limits: Cannot guarantee compliance. A managed CLAUDE.md is guidance only; use managed settings permissions.deny, sandbox.enabled, env for enforcement. For system-prompt-level instructions use --append-system-prompt (set at launch; better for scripts).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (CLAUDE.md vs auto memory; Troubleshoot; Manage CLAUDE.md for large teams)

facts.behavior: Listed broadest to most specific: Managed policy (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md; Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md; Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md), user ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, project ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, local ./CLAUDE.local.md. Files are concatenated, not overriding: ordered from filesystem root down to the working directory, so closer files are read last; within a directory CLAUDE.local.md is appended after CLAUDE.md. CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory and every directory above it load at launch. Those in subdirectories load on demand once Claude reads, writes or edits a file there (including single-file cat/head Bash reads).
facts.limits: Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files do not appear under Memory files in /context at launch. Contradicting instructions: "Claude may pick one arbitrarily." Whole file loads if <=4 MiB; a file over 4 MiB is skipped entirely (loads none of it).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Choose where to put CLAUDE.md files; How CLAUDE.md files load)

facts.behavior: "target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence." If an instruction file is over the recommended length you see a warning at startup and in /status; a warning also appears when files each within length add up past a combined limit at session start. Each CLAUDE.md, rules file, and @path import counts as a separate file.
facts.limits: The 200 lines is a recommendation, not a truncation; the only hard cap for launch-loaded CLAUDE.md is 4 MiB (skipped, not truncated). The exact combined limit number is not stated on the page.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Write effective instructions; My CLAUDE.md is too large)

facts.feature: Per-file limit for on-demand files (subdirectory CLAUDE.md, path-scoped rules)
facts.behavior: When a subdirectory CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md (and their @imports), rules in a subdirectory's .claude/rules/, or path-scoped rules (project or ~/.claude/rules) exceed a per-file limit, "Claude receives only the start of it," followed by a note to read the rest with the Read tool. Limit: 40,000 characters on a 200K context window; on 1M window 200,000 characters on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, 150,000 on later models. Applies from v2.1.309.
facts.limits: Applies only to files that load on demand, not launch-loaded CLAUDE.md or unscoped rules. Later instructions are absent from context until Claude chooses to Read.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Claude ignores the end of my subdirectory CLAUDE.md)

facts.behavior: "Your private preferences for this project, loaded alongside CLAUDE.md" and "treated the same way"; located at project root; create manually and add to .gitignore. Loaded at launch from working directory and above; subdirectory ones load on demand. Appended after CLAUDE.md in each directory. A gitignored CLAUDE.local.md exists only in the worktree where created; to share across worktrees import a file from home (@~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md). With CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1, /init's personal option creates and gitignores it.
facts.limits: Not auto-gitignored by Claude Code on creation (manual). Skipped if 'local' excluded from --setting-sources. Its presence counts as a CLAUDE.md for the AGENTS.md check, so AGENTS.md is then not read by default. Docs list it as 'Not shown' in the .claude explorer; sits at project root, not inside .claude/.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Import additional files; Choose where to put); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md (What's not shown)

facts.behavior: "CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using @path/to/import syntax. Imported files are expanded and loaded into context alongside the CLAUDE.md that references them." Relative or absolute paths; relative resolve against the importing file. Recursive, "maximum depth of four hops." Spaces in paths need a backslash; quoted paths are not imported. Import parsing skips code spans and fenced code blocks (wrap in backticks to keep literal).
facts.limits: Imports organize but do not reduce context cost ("imported files load together with the CLAUDE.md"). External imports (resolving outside working directory) in project-level memory files trigger a one-time approval dialog per project; if declined they stay disabled. User-scope files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/rules/) load imports without the dialog, except in Cowork desktop sessions where out-of-directory imports are skipped.

facts.behavior: Block-level HTML comments (<!-- ... -->) are stripped before injection into Claude's context, so they cost no context tokens. Comments inside code blocks are preserved; they remain visible when the file is opened with the Read tool.
facts.limits: Only block-level comments; not stripped in code blocks.

facts.behavior: Markdown files in .claude/rules/ discovered recursively (subdirectories allowed). Rules without paths frontmatter "are loaded at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md." User-level rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to all projects and load before project rules. Supports symlinks (circular detected); a symlink target outside the working directory is treated like an external import needing approval, and only rules without paths load after approval. Network-path symlinks (UNC, /net, /Network) are not followed.
facts.limits: "Neither set overrides the other: if a user rule and a project rule conflict, Claude may follow either." Rules are advisory context like CLAUDE.md. Excluded if 'project' excluded from --setting-sources.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Organize rules with .claude/rules/; Share rules with symlinks; User-level rules)

facts.behavior: A rule with YAML paths: globs loads "when Claude uses the Read, Write, or Edit tool on a matching file" or views it via a single-file Bash read like cat/head. Patterns relative to the rule's base directory (project root for project rules; primary working directory for user rules). Brace expansion supported; budget of 1,000 expanded patterns and 4 MiB per rule's paths list. paths is the only frontmatter field Claude Code reads from a rule; others ignored without error; frontmatter is stripped before loading. Unparseable YAML: rule loads as if no paths.
facts.limits: Not loaded at launch; load only on a file Read/Write/Edit/cat/head (not on merely listing or Grep, per docs wording). Do not persist across compaction: they load into message history and are summarized away, reloaded only when a matching file is touched again. "If a rule must persist across compaction, drop the paths: frontmatter or move it to the project-root CLAUDE.md." Sibling-worktree files need session started in that worktree or /cd. Subject to per-file on-demand size limit.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Path-specific rules; Rule frontmatter reference); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window.md (What survives compaction)

Unavailable on versions before v2.1.277, when the built-in plugin is disabled, or sometimes first session after upgrade.

facts.behavior: --add-dir grants file access; "By default, CLAUDE.md files from these directories are not loaded." Setting CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 loads CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md and CLAUDE.local.md from them (CLAUDE.local.md skipped if local excluded from --setting-sources).
facts.limits: /add-dir: "Most .claude/ configuration isn't discovered from the added directory." AGENTS.md in added dirs does not load.

facts.behavior: Notes Claude writes itself; four types recorded in frontmatter type: user, feedback, project, reference. Claude skips what it can derive from the codebase or what CLAUDE.md already says, and "doesn't save something every session" (its own judgment). On by default in local sessions; self-hosted environment sessions default off outside Claude Tag. Toggle in /memory saves autoMemoryEnabled to ~/.claude/settings.json; can be set per project in project settings; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 disables via env. Claude writes a modified ISO 8601 timestamp into frontmatter of memory files it writes that start with YAML frontmatter.
facts.limits: Toggle cannot turn it back on in background sessions or sessions started by another Claude Code session. Machine-local; not shared across machines or cloud environments. Main conversation's auto memory is not loaded into subagents (exception: fork); a subagent's own memory (memory frontmatter field) is a separate directory. What Claude saves is discretionary, not guaranteed.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Auto memory; Enable or disable auto memory)

facts.behavior: ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ containing MEMORY.md index plus one topic file per memory. <project> derives from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories of one repo share one directory; outside git, project root is used. CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME (v2.1.234+) overrides the directory name with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. autoMemoryDirectory setting (absolute path or ~/) relocates it; read from user, project, local, policy or --settings scope.
facts.limits: If autoMemoryDirectory is set in project .claude/settings(.local).json it is honored only under the same workspace-trust rule as hooks; with permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories on, no auto memory is loaded from or saved to a directory chosen by a repository-supplied settings file.

facts.feature: MEMORY.md index load limit and reminder
facts.behavior: "The first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start." After Claude writes to MEMORY.md, Claude Code measures it against the 200-line and 25KB limits; if near a limit it reminds Claude to shorten it (one line per entry, move detail to topic files, merge or drop stale entries). If over a limit the write still succeeds but Claude Code returns an error telling Claude to rewrite the index, "because everything past the limit is dropped on the next load."
facts.limits: Limit applies only to MEMORY.md, not CLAUDE.md. Topic files are not loaded at startup; Claude reads them on demand with file tools. Does not block the write. The shortening is done by Claude acting on the reminder, not by Claude Code itself.

facts.behavior: The cleanupPeriodDays sweep does not delete memory files in projects/<project>/memory/; "MEMORY.md and topic files stay until you or Claude edits or deletes them." Claude Code removes the directory only if it has been empty for the whole retention period. Before v2.1.228 the sweep could delete old files beneath it.
facts.limits: Deleted by claude purge (transcripts and auto memory for a project) or by deleting ~/.claude/projects/ ("auto memory for every project").

facts.behavior: "Edit CLAUDE.md files, enable or disable auto memory, and view auto memory entries." Lists CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and other memory file locations across user and project scopes (including entries for files that do not exist yet; selecting one creates it), provides an auto memory toggle and an option to open the auto memory folder; opens selected file in editor. Can show AGENTS.md path if read directly (v2.1.280+).
facts.limits: Docs say to use /context (not /memory) to check which CLAUDE.md and rules files loaded at launch. Asking Claude to 'remember' something saves to auto memory, not CLAUDE.md; say 'add this to CLAUDE.md' to write CLAUDE.md.

facts.behavior: "Initialize project with a CLAUDE.md guide." Analyzes the codebase and generates a starting CLAUDE.md (build commands, test instructions, conventions). If a CLAUDE.md exists it suggests improvements rather than overwriting. With CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 it is an interactive multi-phase flow asking which artifacts to set up (CLAUDE.md files, skills, hooks, personal memory file), explores with a subagent and presents a reviewable proposal before writing. If it finds OpenAI Codex or Google Gemini CLI config it offers to carry it over with /import.
facts.limits: Generates starting content only; does not enforce anything. Default (non-interactive) flow is not the multi-phase one.

facts.behavior: Bundled skill: "Run a setup checkup that diagnoses installation, settings, extension, and CLAUDE.md problems and proposes fixes that Claude applies after you confirm." Alias /checkup. Covers installation health, extensions (unused skills, MCP servers, plugins vs context cost; slow hooks), CLAUDE.md files (local duplicating checked-in, derivable checked-in content such as directory layouts, dependency lists, architecture overviews, and offers to migrate always-loaded guidance into skills and on-demand nested CLAUDE.md), permissions (offer to make auto mode default, pre-approve read-only commands), and usage (v2.1.305+, last 7 days, omitted while Remote Control connected). 'Claude reports its findings first and asks for confirmation before changing anything.' `claude doctor` in a terminal is read-only installation diagnostics without a session.
facts.limits: It is a prompt handed to Claude, run on demand, not a continuous check or gate. Changes only after confirmation.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands.md (/doctor); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md (Check your setup with /doctor); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (My CLAUDE.md is too large)

facts.behavior: "Claude looks for problems such as instructions written for older models, references to files or commands that don't exist, and files that contradict each other. You get a report of findings with proposed edits, and nothing in your files changes until you ask Claude to apply them." Default scope: CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md plus rules, skills, commands, subagents and output styles under .claude/ and ~/.claude/. Optional path argument narrows scope (e.g. /doctor prompt-audit .claude/skills/deploy). Requires v2.1.283+. Runs through the bundled /claude-api skill.
facts.limits: Unavailable when /claude-api is turned off via skillOverrides or disableBundledSkills. Read-only report; model judgment, not a deterministic linter. Manual invocation only.

facts.behavior: "Visualize current context usage as a colored grid. Shows optimization suggestions for context-heavy tools, memory bloat, and capacity warnings." Lists loaded CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and auto memory files under Memory files; warns when conversation exceeds the context window. In fullscreen mode per-item breakdown collapses; /context all expands.
facts.limits: Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files (loaded on demand) are not listed at launch; a 'Loaded' line appears in the terminal when they load. Diagnostic only; changes nothing.

facts.behavior: Before you type: CLAUDE.md (or AGENTS.md), auto memory, MCP tool names, and skill descriptions load into context. Output style and --append-system-prompt text may add more. Path-scoped rules load when matching files are touched; subagents run in their own context window and return only a summary plus metadata trailer.
facts.limits: Skill bodies load only when invoked (or judged relevant); only descriptions are always present. Docs say rules without paths load every session.

facts.behavior: Re-injected from disk: project-root CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules; auto memory; plan-mode plan; skill descriptions (v2.1.304+). System prompt and output style still apply. Invoked skill bodies re-injected capped at 5,000 tokens per skill and 25,000 total, oldest dropped first (truncation keeps start of file). Up to five most recently modified files re-read; files over 5,000 tokens return as path reference only. Git status snapshot refreshed. SessionStart hooks matching the compact source run and add output. Background commands and subagents keep running.
facts.limits: Rules with paths: and nested subdirectory CLAUDE.md are summarized away and reload only on demand. Context hooks added earlier is summarized. Conversation-only instructions are lost; "Add conversation-only instructions to CLAUDE.md to make them persist."
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window.md (What survives compaction); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Instructions seem lost after /compact)

facts.behavior: /compact [instructions] summarizes the conversation to free context, optional focus instructions. Claude Code compacts automatically as context nears the limit. /autocompact [auto|<tokens>] (v2.1.221+) sets how full the window gets before auto-compaction, saved to user settings. /rewind then 'Summarize from here/up to here' compacts part of the conversation. Idle conversations may also compact (idleCompaction setting). 1M-token window supported on Fable models, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.6 and later, Sonnet 4.6. Summarization inherits session extended-thinking config (v2.1.198+).
facts.limits: Per-model default thresholds are in model-config.md (not fetched). Automatic summary is Claude's guess of what matters.

facts.behavior: "Start a new conversation with empty context." Optional name labels the previous conversation in /resume picker. Aliases /reset, /new. Previous conversation resumable via /resume.
facts.limits: Does not continue the same conversation (use /compact for that). CLAUDE.md and memory reload as in any new session.

facts.behavior: "Custom commands have been merged into skills. A file at .claude/commands/deploy.md and a skill at .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy and work the same way. Your existing .claude/commands/ files keep working." commands/*.md is described as the older, single-file format; prefer a skill for new work (supporting files). Command files accept the skill frontmatter fields except name and paths. Command files in subfolders namespace (frontend/component.md -> /frontend:component). When a skill and a .claude/commands/ file share a name, the skill wins. Both live at project and global scope and are committed.
facts.limits: Commands cannot set name or paths and have no supporting-file directory. The skills.md page was read only to ~100,000 of ~118,821 characters.

facts.feature: Bundled skills and workflows in the command list
facts.behavior: commands.md marks entries as built-in (behavior coded in the CLI), Skill (a bundled skill: 'a prompt handed to Claude', works like skills you write) or Workflow (bundled dynamic workflow fanning out across subagents in background). Marked Skills include /batch, /claude-api, /debug, /doctor, /loop, /simplify; /deep-research is a Workflow; /verify runs only when invoked. Commands are recognized only at the start of a message; up to six skills can be chained in one message. Commands sent mid-response queue until the turn ends, except some (e.g. /status, /tasks, /usage) run immediately. MCP servers can expose prompts that appear as commands. Commands unavailable to you are hidden; a few (e.g. /heapdump) hidden by design until full name typed.
facts.limits: Skill-type commands are model prompts, not deterministic code. /agents on v2.1.198+ only prints a reminder (interactive UI removed after v2.1.197). /review is an alias of /code-review (v2.1.223+).
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands.md (All commands; How the command menu matches; MCP prompts)

facts.feature: Other built-in commands relevant to configuration
facts.behavior: /hooks: view hook configurations. /permissions (alias /allowed-tools): manage allow, ask, deny rules by scope, working directories, auto mode denials. /skills: list skills; toggle visibility to Claude and the / menu; cannot cycle plugin skills, disable-model-invocation skills, or skills overridden in managed settings/--settings. /config (alias /settings) [key=value]: opens Settings or sets keys directly, also in -p mode; cannot turn on settings needing panel confirmation. /status: Settings Status tab with version, model, account, connectivity, Session kind. /add-dir, /cd. /output-style [style] (v2.1.269+). /rewind (aliases /checkpoint, /undo). /usage (aliases /cost, /stats). /insights writes HTML report. /export. /security-review (needs origin remote). /sandbox toggles sandbox mode.
facts.limits: /hooks only views, does not edit. Behavior of output styles (append vs replace system prompt) and permission-rule visibility into MCP calls are not covered by the four assigned pages.

facts.behavior: Project-scope under repo .claude/ (committed): CLAUDE.md or ./CLAUDE.md, rules/*.md, settings.json, skills/<name>/SKILL.md, commands/*.md, output-styles/*.md, agents/*.md, workflows/*.js (saved from /workflows; each file becomes a /<name> command), agent-memory/<name>/ (subagent persistent memory). Project-only: settings.local.json (personal overrides, "gitignored when Claude Code saves a setting to it"), .mcp.json and .worktreeinclude at repo root (committed). Global ~/.claude: same families plus ~/.claude.json (app state, account, UI toggles, personal MCP servers; not committed), projects/<project>/memory/ (auto memory), keybindings.json, themes/*.json. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates ~/.claude and ~/.claude.json. Managed-settings.json is system-level and overrides user/project settings and --settings apart from narrow exceptions. Frontmatter fields per file type are tabulated (rules read only paths).
facts.limits: Docs say rules paths are the only rule frontmatter. Agents shipped in plugins honor only a subset of subagent fields. CLAUDE.local.md and AGENTS.md live outside the explorer. Plugins live in ~/.claude/plugins.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md (File reference; Frontmatter fields by file; What's not shown)

facts.behavior: "Claude Code deletes the files in the paths below once they're older than cleanupPeriodDays"; default 30 days, minimum 1, 0 fails validation. Swept paths under ~/.claude: projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl transcripts (and orphaned/superseded copies), subagents/, tool-results/, mcp-tasks/; file-history/ (pre-edit snapshots, 100 most recent checkpoints); plans/; debug/; paste-cache/; image-cache/; uploads/; dev-mods/; session-env/; tasks/; shell-snapshots/; backups/ (keeps five newest); feedback-bundles/; feedback/drafts/ (shorter of cleanupPeriodDays or 30 days; 10-draft queue); usage-data/; skills/.trash and plugins/.trash; legacy todos/ statsig/ logs/. Same cutoff applies to orphaned worktrees. Session scratchpad is deleted with its transcript.
facts.limits: Sweep skipped in bare mode (claude -p --bare) and paused if retention period cannot be safely determined (warning in /status for unreadable settings). Managed cleanupPeriodDays is honored. Claude Desktop/Cowork transcripts kept at any age unless desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays (v2.1.248+) is set. sessions/ files removed on session exit. Does not delete auto memory.

facts.feature: Kept until you delete them, and plaintext storage
facts.behavior: Not removed by the sweep: history.jsonl (prompt history; entries older than cleanupPeriodDays removed only under HIPAA configuration), stats-cache.json, remote-settings.json (re-fetched), cache/changelog.md, policy-limits.json. State files to keep: .credentials.json, agent-memory/, jobs/ and daemon/. Transcripts and history are "not encrypted at rest. OS file permissions are the only protection"; a credential printed by a command or read from .env is written to the session .jsonl, which also holds system prompt, tool definitions and loaded CLAUDE.md. Mitigations: lower cleanupPeriodDays, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY, --no-session-persistence with -p, persistSession:false (TS SDK only), permission rules denying reads of credential files.
facts.limits: No Python SDK equivalent for persistSession. Deleting projects/ loses resume/rewind and all auto memory.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md (Kept until you delete them; Plaintext storage)

facts.behavior: Deletes state for one project: transcripts and auto memory under projects/, per-session tasks/debug/file-history, matching prompt lines in history.jsonl, and the project's entry in ~/.claude.json. Prints the plan and asks confirmation; --dry-run previews, --yes skips prompt, --all purges every project (deletes history.jsonl outright), -i steps item by item. Named claude project purge before v2.1.288.
facts.limits: Leaves shell-snapshots/ and backups/ (not project-scoped), pasted images and scratchpads under the temp directory, and any /heapdump .heapsnapshot files. Irreversible.

facts.behavior: Per-session directory for temporary files, usable without permission prompts, at /private/tmp/claude-<uid>/<project>/<session-id>/scratchpad/ on macOS (outside ~/.claude); deleted with the session transcript by the sweep; hooks receive scratchpad_dir.
facts.limits: Exists only when signed in with claude.ai (not API key), using Anthropic API (not Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry), and enableArtifact not false. OS may clear it on restart; claude purge does not touch it.

unreachable: None of the four assigned pages 404'd (memory.md, commands.md, claude-directory.md, context-window.md all fetched). Extra: skills.md was read only to character 100,000 of 118,821. Not fetched (linked but out of scope): model-config.md default auto-compact thresholds, errors.md memory-index-is-over-its-read-limit, settings-reference.md cleanupPeriodDays, hooks InstructionsLoaded. Output styles, MCP permission-rule visibility and headless hook behavior are not covered by these four pages. The claude-directory.md explorer is interactive, so only its written tables were captured.

area: MCP servers: scopes, .mcp.json, project approval, tool search, permission rules, managed MCP, hooks on MCP calls (as of 2026-11-03)

facts.behavior: Three scopes: local (default; stored in ~/.claude.json under the project path, private), project (.mcp.json in project root, shared via version control), user (~/.claude.json, all projects). Precedence when the same server is defined more than once: local, project, user, plugin-provided, claude.ai connectors; 'The entire server entry from that source is used; fields are not merged across scopes.' Managed-settings managedMcpServers (v2.1.259+) rank above all. Scopes match by name; plugins/connectors match by endpoint. CLI: claude mcp add -s/--scope <local|user|project>, default local.
facts.limits: No field merging across scopes. Not a policy mechanism by itself.

facts.behavior: File with top-level mcpServers. ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expand in command, args, env, url, headers. Unset var with no default: config still loads with a warning and the literal ${VAR} text. Credential variables (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, HTTPS_PROXY, NPM_TOKEN) are read as empty in a remote server's url/headers; a :-default on them is ignored.
facts.limits: Expansion is not a secret store; other names like API_KEY expand as written. Managed-settings managedMcpServers entries do NOT expand ${VAR} (entries containing it are dropped).

facts.behavior: 'Claude Code prompts for approval in interactive sessions before using project-scoped servers from .mcp.json files.' claude mcp list/get show unapproved ones as 'Pending approval' and do not connect. claude mcp reset-project-choices resets all approved and rejected project-scoped choices. Settings keys enableAllProjectMcpServers, enabledMcpjsonServers, disabledMcpjsonServers record choices (enabledMcpjsonServers/disabledMcpjsonServers are separate from enabledMcpServers/disabledMcpServers, which are the per-project /mcp toggle stored in ~/.claude.json).
facts.limits: No prompt in claude -p, Agent SDK sessions and cloud sessions: 'it loads project-scoped servers without asking' (permissions page: connected without asking, approved or not; SDK loads them only when settingSources includes project). Also skipped in bypassPermissions when skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt is set in user/managed settings. To keep a server out headless: disabledMcpjsonServers (blocks in every permission mode), --setting-sources/settingSources, --bare, or --strict-mcp-config.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md ; claude mcp list --help ; claude mcp reset-project-choices --help

facts.feature: Workspace trust and self-approval of .mcp.json servers
facts.behavior: 'A cloned repository can't approve its own servers: enableAllProjectMcpServers or enabledMcpjsonServers committed to the project's .claude/settings.json is ignored in an untrusted folder, and the server stays at Pending approval.' Approvals from user ~/.claude/settings.json, managed settings and --settings still apply in untrusted folders. 'A disabledMcpjsonServers entry in any settings file still rejects the server.'
facts.limits: Applies to interactive sessions; headless sessions connect without asking. headersHelper on a project .mcp.json/local server runs only after the trust dialog is accepted (headless: never run, static headers only).

facts.behavior: --strict-mcp-config: 'Claude Code then uses only the MCP servers you pass with --mcp-config.' Servers from --mcp-config are still filtered by allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers (except in-process type sdk). With a readable managed-mcp.json deployed, --mcp-config makes a workstation exit at startup ('You cannot dynamically configure MCP servers when an enterprise MCP config is present'); --strict-mcp-config also exits.
facts.limits: --strict-mcp-config limits which config files load; it does not bypass allow/deny lists. Without managed-mcp.json, a --mcp-config server with the same name replaces a managedMcpServers one for that run.

facts.behavior: claude mcp: add (-t stdio|sse|http, -s local|user|project, -e, -H, --client-id, --client-secret, --callback-port), add-json, add-from-claude-desktop (Mac/WSL), get, list, login, logout, remove, reset-project-choices, serve (start Claude Code itself as a stdio MCP server).
facts.limits: claude mcp serve exposes Claude Code's tools only; the connecting MCP client is responsible for user confirmation of individual tool calls. add/remove are blocked by managed policy where applicable.

facts.behavior: 'Tool search is enabled by default: MCP tools are deferred and discovered on demand.' Only tool names and server instructions load at session start. ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: unset/true = all deferred; auto = defer only when definitions reach 10% of context; auto:N = custom percent 0-100; false = load all upfront. Per-server 'alwaysLoad': true loads that server's tools upfront regardless of ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH (makes startup wait up to 5s connect timeout); 'alwaysLoad': false keeps all its tools deferred (v2.1.287+). Server authors can set _meta['anthropic/alwaysLoad'] per tool (user config can override). Denying the ToolSearch tool (permissions.deny: ["ToolSearch"]) makes MCP tools load upfront. Server instructions truncated to 4,096 chars and upfront tool descriptions to 4,096; tools loaded via search keep 16,384 (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH overrides, v2.1.280+).
facts.limits: Only on Opus 4 / Sonnet 4 / Haiku 4.5 and later; earlier models load everything upfront and ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true does not override. Not supported on Microsoft Foundry on Azure; off under CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS (org can keep it on via managed settings, v2.1.227+) and in HIPAA configuration. Deferral concerns context loading only, not permissions. No fixed per-server tool cap. MCP tools whose full name exceeds 128 characters are omitted.

facts.feature: Permission rule syntax for MCP tools
facts.behavior: 'To match every tool from an MCP server, write mcp__<server>__*. To match one tool, write its full name, mcp__<server>__<tool>.' mcp__puppeteer (bare) matches the whole server. Allow rules accept globs only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix (mcp__github__get_*); unanchored allow globs like "*" or "mcp__*" are skipped and auto-approve nothing. Deny and ask rules accept full-name globs, e.g. deny "mcp__*" removes every MCP tool from Claude's context. Server names with . or spaces become _ in rules; plugin servers use mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__*; claude.ai connectors appear as mcp__claude_ai_<server>__<tool>.
facts.limits: Rules see only the tool name, not arguments: 'To match a parameter on an MCP tool, pass a deny rule with --disallowedTools. When Claude Code loads a settings file, it skips any mcp__ rule that has parentheses' (listed in invalid-settings dialog and claude doctor). Tool(param:value) works only on built-in tools. A server containing __ or ending _ needs the wildcard form.

facts.feature: Per-tool forced approval (requiresUserInteraction) and org 'ask' on connector tools
facts.behavior: A server author can set _meta['anthropic/requiresUserInteraction']: true (JSON boolean true only) on a tool: Claude Code prompts on every call, even in acceptEdits, auto and bypassPermissions; no 'don't ask again'; matching allow rules do not skip it; in dontAsk mode the call is denied. Org-set 'ask' on claude.ai connector tools behaves the same (reason 'Your organization requires approval for this tool').
facts.limits: A PreToolUse hook returning allow (with or without updatedInput) cannot skip this prompt. Org 'ask' does not reach Claude Code in desktop app local/SSH sessions (ordinary permission rules apply there instead).

facts.behavior: If deployed, Claude Code loads only: servers in the file, managedMcpServers servers, in-process servers registered by the host app, and optionally built-in Claude in Chrome. Users 'can't add, modify, or use any other MCP servers, including plugin-provided servers and servers passed with --mcp-config'; claude.ai connectors it fetches are suppressed unless allowAllClaudeAiMcps: true. Paths: macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-mcp.json; Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/managed-mcp.json; Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-mcp.json. Same format as .mcp.json. An empty mcpServers map disables MCP. claude mcp add then fails with 'enterprise MCP configuration is active and has exclusive control'.
facts.limits: Standalone file; cannot be delivered through server-managed settings. Readable by any user on the machine (no secrets in env). deniedMcpServers still applies to its servers; servers skip allowedMcpServers unless they use ${VAR} outside env. Claude in Chrome blocked unless allowClaudeInChromeWithManagedMcp (device-level managed settings only, v2.1.282+). Removed servers disappear silently.

facts.behavior: Provides remote (http/sse, https only) servers to every user alongside their own (v2.1.259+). Takes precedence over same-named local/project/user servers. Users cannot edit or remove them (claude mcp remove refuses) but can toggle them off for themselves in /mcp. Entries with command/args/env/headersHelper, ${VAR}, or invalid names are dropped with a /status notice.
facts.limits: Read only from managed sources (server-managed settings, gateway policy, MDM, HKLM, managed-settings.json); the key is dropped with a warning in user/project/local settings. Headers are readable by users. Not honored in Claude Desktop Code tab third-party deployment or Cowork. deniedMcpServers still applies; a -p run keeps a removed server until it ends.

facts.behavior: Entries match by serverUrl (wildcards), serverCommand (exact command+args array; env not compared) or serverName (exact, no wildcards). Evaluation order: merge lists from all scopes, then denylist ('Nothing overrides a denylist match'), then allowlist. allowedMcpServers unset = all allowed; [] = none; populated = only matches (remote servers need a serverUrl match if any serverUrl entries exist; stdio need serverCommand match if any exist; serverName counts only otherwise). Without allowManagedMcpServersOnly, allowlists from all scopes merge (user can broaden); with it true (managed sources only) user/project/local allowlists are ignored. Denylists always merge from every scope. Applies to --mcp-config servers and plugin/connector servers; re-checked on reconnect.
facts.limits: 'A serverName entry, in either list, is not a security control' (user picks the name); use serverUrl/serverCommand to enforce. allowManagedMcpServersOnly is separate from allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly (the latter does not enforce the MCP allowlist). Exempt from allowlist: managedMcpServers, managed-mcp.json entries without ${VAR} outside env, built-in servers (ide, Claude in Chrome), in-process type sdk servers (skip all three checks). Env-var expansion in policy entries uses a pinned environment (v2.1.219+). Blocked servers vanish silently from /mcp. Allowlist reading across sources needs v2.1.273+.

facts.behavior: strictPluginOnlyCustomization with mcp in the list: users cannot add servers via ~/.claude.json or .mcp.json; only plugin servers (and managedMcpServers) load. disableClaudeAiConnectors / ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false turn off claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself (any-source-true semantics). OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 records MCP server/tool names in telemetry.
facts.limits: Connectors delivered in desktop app local/SSH sessions arrive as in-process sdk servers; no MCP setting or managed-mcp.json reaches them (governed in claude.ai org settings). Cloud sessions are filtered by allow/deny lists delivered to the session.

facts.behavior: MCP tools are named mcp__<server>__<tool> and appear in PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied. facts.feature: PreToolUse hooks on MCP calls: input, decisions, blocking
facts.behavior: PreToolUse 'runs after Claude creates tool parameters and before processing the tool call' and matches any tool name including MCP tools. Input: tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id; for MCP tools also mcp_server {name, source} (v2.1.274+; 'Base trust decisions on source rather than on name or the mcp__<server>__ prefix'). Output hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: allow skips the permission prompt; deny prevents the call; ask prompts; defer ends the turn (non-interactive -p only, single tool call only). updatedInput replaces the entire input object before execution, and permission rules are evaluated against the updated input. Precedence among hooks: deny > defer > ask > allow. Exit code 2 blocks the call like deny (stderr shown to Claude), even if JSON says allow.
facts.limits: 'Deny and ask rules are still evaluated regardless of what the hook returns' (allow does not override a deny rule). allow does not skip the prompt for MCP tools marked requiresUserInteraction, org-'ask' connector tools, or actions no mode auto-approves. PreToolUse does not fire for @-referenced files or non-tool paths. Only fires when Claude calls a tool.

facts.behavior: Blocking is per event (PreToolUse can block; PostToolUse cannot undo). 'On most events, when a hook fails or times out, Claude Code still carries out the action.' command/http hooks accept "onFailure": "block" to make failures block (v2.1.295+). Default timeouts: 600s command/http/mcp_tool, 30s prompt, 60s agent; timed-out hooks are cancelled and output discarded. Non-2 nonzero exit is non-blocking.
facts.limits: Without onFailure: block, a crashing or timed-out PreToolUse hook does not block the MCP call. The hook 'if' filter is best-effort: 'use the permission system rather than a hook to enforce a hard allow or deny.' Hooks cannot see argument-level rules in the permission system, but hooks can inspect tool_input of MCP calls themselves.

facts.behavior: Fires after successful completion with tool_input, tool_response and mcp_server. updatedToolOutput replaces what Claude sees (all tools); updatedMCPToolOutput replaces output for MCP tools only ('Prefer updatedToolOutput'). decision: block adds reason next to the result. MCP output is passed through without schema validation.
facts.limits: Tool has already run; cannot undo side effects. Exit 2 only shows stderr to Claude. Changes only what Claude sees.

facts.feature: Hook type mcp_tool (hooks that call an MCP tool)

On blocking events (PreToolUse, Stop) Claude Code waits for a connecting server up to MCP_TIMEOUT. isError:true results are non-blocking errors.
facts.limits: Never starts OAuth. Skipped for SessionStart at launch and Setup events (servers not yet available). Does not wait on observational events.

facts.behavior: "Add the -p (or --print) flag to any claude command to run it non-interactively." Exits 0 on success and non-zero on failure. Invalid flags are reported to stderr before the run starts; in-run failures such as missing auth are printed as the result on stdout. Without --bare, a -p session "discovers and loads [hooks, skills, commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, CLAUDE.md] as an interactive session would, including anything configured in the working directory or ~/.claude."
facts.limits: Not every CLI option combines with -p: --bg is rejected, and --cloud with a task description is rejected. Built-in terminal-only commands such as /login are unavailable. Piped stdin is capped at 10MB. Settings files that fail validation are silently ignored in this mode (no error dialog).

facts.behavior: "skip auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md." claude --help: also skips LSP, plugin sync, attribution, background prefetches, keychain reads; sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1. Claude keeps Bash, file read and file edit tools. Anthropic auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper via --settings (OAuth/keychain never read); Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry use their own credentials. Context must be passed explicitly: --append-system-prompt[-file], --settings, --mcp-config, --agents, --plugin-dir/--plugin-url, --add-dir. Only MCP servers from the command line connect; no system reminders (Claude is not told the skills list, nor when files change on disk); no background commands or background subagents. Docs: "--bare is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for -p in a future release."
facts.limits: A directory given with --add-dir is a partial exception: its .claude/skills/ load but its .claude/commands/ and .claude/agents/ do not. Skills still resolve via /skill-name per --help. The project's env block and helpers such as awsAuthRefresh in settings files still apply, and apiKeyHelper is read only from --settings. Before v2.1.286 these limits held only partly. Does not use subscription login.

facts.behavior: claude --help: "The workspace trust dialog is skipped when Claude is run in non-interactive mode (via -p, or when stdout is not a TTY, e.g. piped or redirected output). Only use this in directories you trust." Docs: "A -p session shows no workspace trust dialog and no per-server approval prompt." Without --bare, -p runs the hooks in the project's .claude/settings.json and connects the servers in its .mcp.json, even in a never-trusted folder. For a never-trusted folder under -p: hooks in settings files, the env block, helpers like apiKeyHelper, and a project skill's hooks and allowed-tools are USED; permissions.allow rules and additionalDirectories in .claude/settings.json are NOT used (stderr warning 'this workspace has not been trusted'); frontmatter hooks in project subagents, project @skills-dir plugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, and inline subagent mcpServers are NOT used; .mcp.json servers are connected without asking, approved or not; a headersHelper is not run.

Nothing gates automatically.

facts.behavior: Settings-file hooks run in a plain -p session (project and user), including in never-trusted folders. --bare skips hooks defined in settings and by installed plugins ("features built into Claude Code are unaffected"). SessionStart and Setup hook events are always included in stream-json output; --include-hook-events adds other hook lifecycle events (requires --output-format stream-json). --init and --maintenance run Setup hooks with the init/maintenance matcher (print mode only). A PermissionRequest hook can approve a call that would otherwise be denied in a -p Manual-mode run. On SIGTERM only SessionEnd hooks run. --settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}' turns hooks off for the run.
facts.limits: The docs fetched do not state that any specific hook event is skipped in plain -p other than via --bare / disableAllHooks. Some events (Notification, SessionEnd, PreCompact, PostCompact) never produce hook_started even with --include-hook-events.
