facts.behavior: --output-format: text (default), json ("structured JSON with result, session ID, and metadata"), stream-json (newline-delimited JSON for real-time streaming; last line is a result message with final text, cost and session metadata). stream-json with --verbose and --include-partial-messages streams tokens. --input-format: text (default) or stream-json (realtime streaming input). --replay-user-messages needs both stream-json formats. system/init event reports model, tools, MCP servers, plugins, plugin_errors, mcp_server_errors. system/api_retry events are emitted before retries. permission_denied system messages and result.permission_denials appear in stream-json.

facts.behavior: "To get output conforming to a specific schema, use --output-format json with --json-schema." The structured result is in the structured_output field of the JSON response. An invalid schema makes claude exit with 'Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema'.
facts.limits: The format keyword is accepted but treated as an annotation and not enforced. If a run ends without valid structured output (e.g. Claude declined) the structured_output field is absent; scripts must check for it. Print mode only.

facts.behavior: "Limit the number of agentic turns (print mode only). No limit by default." With --input-format stream-json, a message still queued when the limit ends a turn stays queued and starts a new turn with its own limit.

facts.behavior: "Stop the run once estimated spend on API calls reaches this amount (print mode only)." Checked against Claude Code's client-side cost estimate; subagent spend counts toward the cap; the 1.1x data-residency multiplier counts. Once spend reaches the cap, spawning another subagent fails with 'Budget limit reached', and background subagents still running are stopped (v2.1.217+). A run at the cap stops waiting on remaining background work.

facts.behavior: --allowedTools auto-approves listed tools using permission rule syntax (trailing ' *' gives prefix matching; Bash(git diff *) allows any command starting with git diff). "Calls to tools you didn't list run if they need no approval. In a Manual mode claude -p run, a call that needs approval is denied unless something approves it" (a PermissionRequest hook or --permission-prompt-tool). From v2.1.302, -p runs start in Manual mode when nothing sets a mode. --permission-mode accepts acceptEdits, auto, bypassPermissions, manual, dontAsk, plan. dontAsk denies every call that would otherwise prompt (read-only/allowed actions still run; AskUserQuestion, requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, network-path reads, and org-'ask' connector tools are denied even with an allow rule); an installed mod can still approve some. acceptEdits auto-approves file writes and mkdir/touch/mv/cp. In auto mode a bare Bash allow entry is dropped and the classifier evaluates each command.
facts.limits: Bash argument-constraining patterns are fragile (docs warn Bash(curl http://github.com/ *) misses variations). Managed-settings permission rules cannot be overridden by command-line arguments.

facts.behavior: --permission-prompts host (default) sends prompts to the SDK host (canUseTool callback) or --permission-prompt-tool; none denies anything that would prompt, tells Claude nobody can approve and not to retry, removes AskUserQuestion-type tools, and cancels unanswered MCP elicitations. Rules, PermissionRequest hooks and the permission mode still decide first (v2.1.259+; present in installed claude --help). --permission-prompt-tool takes a full mcp__<server>__<tool> name of an MCP tool to answer prompts in non-interactive mode.
facts.limits: The prompt tool cannot approve an MCP tool marked requiresUserInteraction (allow converted to deny, v2.1.199+).

facts.feature: Permission rules and MCP tool calls
facts.behavior: MCP tools are matched by name only: mcp__server, mcp__server__*, or mcp__server__tool. "To match a parameter on an MCP tool, pass a deny rule with --disallowedTools. When Claude Code loads a settings file, it skips any mcp__ rule that has parentheses." Skipped rules are listed in the invalid-settings dialog (interactive) and claude doctor. --disallowedTools: a bare name removes the tool from Claude's context ('mcp__*' removes every MCP tool); a scoped rule leaves the tool and denies matching calls. Allow globs are accepted only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix; unanchored allow globs like mcp__* are skipped. Deny/ask accept bare-name globs.
facts.limits: A settings-file rule cannot constrain MCP tool arguments; parenthesised mcp__ rules are skipped. Only the --disallowedTools CLI flag route is described for parameter matching on MCP tools. permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories does not limit shell commands, MCP tools, or hook programs.
facts.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md ('Match by input parameter', MCP section, line 'To match a parameter on an MCP tool') ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference.md (--disallowedTools)

facts.behavior: --append-system-prompt[-file] adds to the default prompt, keeping tool guidance, safety instructions and coding conventions. --system-prompt[-file] replaces the default prompt entirely: "Replacing drops all of the default prompt, including tool guidance and safety instructions" and also drops the git status snapshot. --append-subagent-system-prompt[-file] (-p only) appends to every subagent's prompt (not forked subagents). --system-prompt-snapshot on|off: by default the rendered prompt (including --system-prompt/--append) is recorded on the first request and reused verbatim on later requests and resumes, even if a later launch passes different text, until compaction; off under --bare unless forced on. --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections moves cwd/env/memory paths/git status into the first user message for cache reuse (default prompt only). For persistent personas docs point to output styles; for project conventions CLAUDE.md.

facts.behavior: --continue resumes the most recent conversation; --resume takes a session ID, name, or absolute path to a .jsonl transcript; session IDs can be captured from json output (.session_id). claude -p --continue includes -p, SDK and /loop sessions (plain --continue skips them). --no-session-persistence (print mode only) keeps sessions off disk so they cannot be resumed. --session-id <uuid> sets a specific ID; --fork-session makes a new ID on resume. --continue/--resume reports total_cost_usd for the whole conversation including earlier runs.

facts.feature: Headless run lifecycle: background work, SIGTERM, deleted cwd
facts.behavior: After the turn finishes and stdin closes, a -p run waits for background commands, subagents/workflows, Monitor watches and pending /loop wakeups (10 minute idle-wait cap by default; CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS, 0 for no cap). MCP tasks and auto-backgrounded MCP calls are not waited on (results lost). SIGTERM exits 143, leaves the in-progress turn unfinished, kills Bash process trees and runs only SessionEnd hooks. If cwd is deleted mid-run the session continues with a stream-json warning.
facts.limits: --bare disables background tasks entirely. 10-minute cap does not end the wait while a main-conversation background command is still running.

facts.behavior: --fallback-model sonnet,haiku: tries listed models in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable. --tools restricts the built-in tool set ('' disables all). --setting-sources user,project,local limits which settings sources load. --settings loads extra settings from file or JSON. --strict-mcp-config uses only --mcp-config servers. With -p, --mcp-config waits for pending servers up to MCP_TIMEOUT (30s default). --restricted removes command-running tools and WebFetch unless named in --tools, ignores user/project/local settings (managed and --settings still apply), confines file tools to working directories, refuses bypassPermissions. --safe-mode disables CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP, custom commands/agents, output styles, workflows, themes, keybindings (managed policy still applies; auth, model, built-in tools and permissions work normally) and sets CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE=1. --dangerously-load-development-channels is ignored with -p. --prompt-suggestions emits prompt_suggestion messages (needs stream-json and --verbose).
